heading: Feudalism
body: A two-player engine-building card game where you collect crop tokens, purchase development cards, and attract patron visitors to earn influence points. The first player to reach 15 influence triggers the final round. The player with the most influence wins!

heading: How to Play
body:
Each turn, choose ONE action:

1. Take Tokens: Click 'Take Tokens' then select up to 3 different crop types from the supply. You must take 3 if 3+ types are available.

2. Take 2 Same: Click a crop button in the 'Take 2' row to take 2 tokens of one type (requires 4+ of that type in the supply).

3. Reserve a Card: Click a market card and choose 'Reserve' to add it to your hand (max 3). You also receive 1 mead (wild) token. You can also click a deck to reserve the top card blind.

4. Purchase a Card: Click a market card and choose 'Buy', or click a reserved card to purchase it. Pay the crop cost minus your card bonuses. Mead tokens can substitute for any crop.

heading: Card Market
body:
The market shows 3 tiers of development cards (4 visible per tier):

Smallholding (bottom): Cheap cards with small or no influence.
Farm (middle): Mid-range cards, 1–3 influence.
Estate (top): Expensive cards, 3–5 influence.

Each card shows:
- Coloured bar: the crop bonus you gain when purchased.
- Number (top-left): influence points.
- Cost (bottom): crops required to purchase.

When a card is purchased or reserved, a new card is drawn from the deck to replace it.

heading: Crop Tokens
body:
There are 5 crop types (4 tokens each for 2 players) plus 5 mead (wild) tokens.

Crop abbreviations:
O = Oats (golden)
F = Flax (blue)
W = Wheat (amber)
B = Barley (pale)
T = Turnip (green)
M = Mead (wild)

You can hold a maximum of 10 tokens. If you exceed this limit after taking tokens, you must discard down to 10.

heading: Patrons
body:
Patron tiles are displayed on the left side. Each requires a certain number of card bonuses (not tokens!) and awards 3 influence points.

Patrons visit automatically at the end of your turn if you meet their requirements. You cannot choose to delay a patron visit.

heading: Winning
body:
When any player reaches 15+ influence points, the current round is completed so both players have equal turns. The player with the most influence wins.

Tiebreaker: The player with fewer purchased development cards wins.

heading: Strategy Tips
body:
- Focus on cards whose bonuses help you buy other cards cheaply (engine building).
- Smallholding cards are cheap and provide bonuses that discount future purchases.
- Track which patrons you're closest to — 3 free influence is valuable.
- Mead tokens are powerful wildcards — reserve strategically to earn them.
- Don't hoard tokens you don't need — you'll hit the 10-token limit.
- Watch what your opponent is collecting and consider blocking key cards.
